extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate / graduate students in complex analysis and Fourier analysis
extracted.subtask_description: Textbook-level theorems, definitions, and identities about branches of the complex logarithm, holomorphic logarithms of nowhere-vanishing functions, power definitions z^α, Fourier series coefficients and mean-value properties, Fourier transform decay/inversion/Poisson summation via contour integration, and the Paley–Wiener characterization of compactly supported transforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of a branch of the logarithm (Theorem 6.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose that Ω is simply connected with 1 ∈ Ω, and 0 ∉ Ω. Then in Ω there is a branch of the logarithm F(z) = log_Ω(z) so that (i) F is holomorphic in Ω, (ii) e^{F(z)} = z for all z ∈ Ω, (iii) F(r) = log r whenever r is a real number and near 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct F as a primitive of 1/z: F(z)=∫_γ (1/w) dw where γ is any curve in Ω connecting 1 to z; path-independence follows from simple connectedness. Then F′(z)=1/z and ze^{-F(z)} is constant (equal to 1 by evaluation at z=1). For real r near 1 choose the straight line path to recover the usual real logarithm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal branch on the slit plane (example)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the slit plane Ω = C  ig ackslash (−∞,0], the principal branch of the logarithm is given by log z = log r + iθ where z = r e^{iθ} with |θ| < π.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses the path of integration composed of the line segment from 1 to r and the arc from r to re^{iθ}; the integral of 1/w along that path yields log r + iθ. Convention: drop the subscript Ω and write simply log z for this principal branch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logarithm is not globally additive
rubrics_metrics.description: In general log(z1 z2) ≠ log z1 + log z2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: with principal branch, if z1 = z2 = e^{2π i/3} then log z1 = log z2 = 2π i/3 but z1 z2 = e^{−2π i/3} so log(z1 z2) = −2π i/3 ≠ log z1 + log z2. Multi-valuedness / branch choices create these discrepancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taylor expansion of log(1+z) (principal branch)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the principal branch, log(1+z) = z − z^2/2 + z^3/3 − ··· = −∑_{n=1}^∞ (−1)^n z^n / n for |z| < 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derive by noting both sides have derivative 1/(1+z) and both vanish at z=0, so they differ by 0. Valid in unit disc for principal branch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of complex powers via a branch of log
rubrics_metrics.description: If Ω is simply connected with 1 ∈ Ω and 0 ∉ Ω, choose the branch of the logarithm with log 1 = 0 and define z^α = e^{α log z} for any α ∈ C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Properties: 1^α = 1. If α = 1/n then (z^{1/n})^n = z provided the same branch/log chosen; the definition relies on a single-valued branch log_Ω.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logarithm of a nowhere-vanishing holomorphic function (Theorem 6.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f is a nowhere vanishing holomorphic function in a simply connected region Ω, then there exists a holomorphic function g on Ω such that f(z) = e^{g(z)}. The function g can be denoted log f(z).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: fix z_0∈Ω and define g(z)=∫_γ f'(w)/f(w) dw + c_0 where γ connects z_0 to z and c_0 chosen so e^{c_0}=f(z_0). Path-independence follows from simple connectedness. Then g′(z)=f′(z)/f(z) and f e^{−g} is constant, equal to 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power series expansion and Cauchy coefficient formula (Theorem 7.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f is holomorphic in a disc D_R(z_0) and f(z)=∑_{n=0}^∞ a_n (z−z_0)^n converges in that disc, then a_n = (1/(2π r^n)) ∫_{0}^{2π} f(z_0 + r e^{iθ}) e^{−i n θ} dθ for all n ≥ 0 and 0<r<R. Moreover the integral equals 0 whenever n<0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derive from Cauchy integral formula with γ the circle z_0 + r e^{iθ}. Interpretation: Fourier coefficients of the restriction of f to a circle vanish for negative indices; positive indices relate to power series coefficients up to factor r^n.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mean-value property for holomorphic functions (Corollary 7.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f is holomorphic in a disc D_R(z_0), then f(z_0) = (1/(2π)) ∫_{0}^{2π} f(z_0 + r e^{iθ}) dθ for any 0 < r < R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain from the n=0 coefficient equality a_0 = f(z_0). Taking real parts gives the same mean-value property for harmonic functions (Corollary 7.3): u(z_0) equals the average of u on any circle centered at z_0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderate decrease and class Fa (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each a>0, Fa is the class of functions f holomorphic in the horizontal strip S_a = {z: |Im(z)| < a} and there exists A>0 with |f(x+iy)| ≤ A/(1+x^2) for all x∈R and |y|<a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation: functions holomorphic in a strip and of uniform moderate decay along horizontal lines. Examples: e^{−π z^2} belongs to Fa for all a; 1/(π(c^2+z^2)) belongs to Fa for 0<a<c; 1/ cosh(π z) ∈ Fa for |a|<1/2. Derivatives inherit similar membership for smaller strips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decay of Fourier transform for functions in Fa (Theorem 2.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f ∈ F_a for some a>0, then |f̂(ξ)| ≤ B e^{−2π b |ξ|} for any 0 ≤ b < a (here f̂(ξ)=∫_{−∞}^{∞} f(x)e^{−2π i x ξ} dx).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof via contour shifting: shift the real line vertically by ±b and estimate integrals over vertical segments (which vanish as radius→∞) to obtain exponential decay of f̂. The larger the strip of analyticity (a), the better decay one can choose (larger b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fourier inversion for F (Theorem 2.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f ∈ F (i.e., belongs to some Fa), then the Fourier inversion formula holds: f(x) = ∫_{−∞}^{∞} f̂(ξ) e^{2π i x ξ} dξ for all x∈R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses contour integration and the identity ∫_0^∞ e^{−(A+iB)ξ} dξ = 1/(A+iB) (Lemma 2.3), together with shifting contours for ξ>0 and ξ<0 and residue/limit arguments to reconstruct f(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: Elementary integral identity (Lemma 2.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A>0 and B∈R, then ∫_0^∞ e^{−(A+iB)ξ} dξ = 1/(A+iB).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used inside inversion proof when integrating over ξ after contour shifts; justification by dominated convergence since integrand is absolutely integrable (decay e^{−Aξ}).

rubrics_metrics.name: Poisson summation formula for F (Theorem 2.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f ∈ F then ∑_{n∈Z} f(n) = ∑_{n∈Z} f̂(n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: consider f(z)/(e^{2π i z}−1) with simple poles at integers (residue f(n)/(2π i)) and apply residue theorem on growing rectangles; shift contours and expand 1/(e^{2π i z}−1) in geometric series depending on |e^{2π i z}|≷1 to obtain sums of f̂(n). Applications: theta-transformation identities and identities for special functions (Gaussian, 1/cosh).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gaussian self-reciprocity and theta identity (used with Poisson summation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Gaussian e^{−π x^2} is its own Fourier transform: ∫ e^{−π x^2} e^{−2π i x ξ} dx = e^{−π ξ^2}. Applying Poisson summation yields theta transformation ϑ(t)=t^{−1/2}ϑ(1/t) (equation (4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By scaling and translating variables one obtains identity (3): ∑_{n∈Z} e^{−π t (n+a)^2} = t^{−1/2} ∑_{n∈Z} e^{−π n^2 / t} e^{2π i n a}, useful for analytic continuation and functional equations (e.g., Riemann zeta).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paley–Wiener characterization (Theorem 3.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose f is continuous and of moderate decrease on R. Then f has an extension to an entire function with |f(z)| ≤ A e^{2π M |z|} for some A>0 iff f̂ is supported in the interval [−M, M].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One direction: if f̂ supported in [−M,M] then f(z)=∫_{−M}^{M} f̂(ξ)e^{2π i ξ z} dξ gives an entire extension with growth ≤ A e^{2π M |Im z|} ≤ A e^{2π M |z|}. Converse: via contour-shift arguments one first proves the stronger bound |f(x+iy)| ≤ A e^{2π M |y|} (and optionally moderate decay in x) to deduce f̂(ξ)=0 for |ξ|>M; auxiliary mollifiers like f_ε(z)=f(z)/(1+iε z)^2 are used to handle decay at infinity and take limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial converse: exponential decay of f̂ implies strip analyticity (Theorem 3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f̂ satisfies |f̂(ξ)| ≤ A e^{−2π a |ξ|} for some a>0, A>0, then f(x) is the restriction to R of a function f(z) holomorphic in the strip S_b = {z: |Im(z)| < b} for any 0<b<a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define f(z)=∫_{−∞}^{∞} f̂(ξ)e^{2π i ξ z} dξ; absolute convergence follows because e^{2π b |ξ|} f̂(ξ) is integrable when b<a. Uniform limits of entire approximants show holomorphy in the strip.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary on uniqueness from support/decay (Corollary 3.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f̂(ξ)=O(e^{−2π a |ξ|}) for some a>0 and f vanishes on a non-empty open interval then f≡0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because f extends analytically to a strip containing the real axis, analyticity plus vanishing on an open set implies f is identically zero. In particular f and f̂ cannot both have compact support unless f=0.
